notes: Template: TBox expansion, fictional relation (a real class with a made-up property). The rule gives every Swiss canton a "beacon city", a relation no model has seen, so the record tests acquiring a new rule and applying it to members the model already knows. Each derived query names a real canton and leaves the membership to the model (inheritance, 2 hops: the inserted rule plus the stored fact that the canton is Swiss, checked before editing). Because the relation is new and has one value everywhere, an editor that learned only "beacon city -> Lucerne" would pass all three derived queries without using the membership; the near unrelated query is the control that separates the two readings. It asks the beacon city of a region outside the class (the German state of Bavaria): a method that applied the rule through membership leaves it unanswered as before, one that learned a bare "beacon city" -> Lucerne mapping answers Lucerne there. Read the derived scores together with this control. Lucerne was chosen as the value rather than Bern, which a model could guess for anything Swiss without the edit; the canton of Lucerne is not asked, since its name would give the answer away. The capital of Ticino (Bellinzona) is not used as a near query: smaller models often answer Lugano, which would make the specificity score noisy. Insert: no original answers, no derivability, determinate only.
